memory_lessons.applicability: Same CUDA n-body kernel and official correctness/timing context; this supports further measurement of tiling but does not predict the compact 128-thread variant's performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The observed 256-thread shared-memory tiling candidate was valid on all 11 correctness cases and measured 0.0010037409 seconds, versus 0.0018473421 seconds for baseline. This comparison does not isolate the cause of the difference or establish a result for other tile configurations.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 128-thread variant under the same official protocol; if it regresses, compare compact source staging with the previously measured 256-thread configuration.

proposal.hypothesis: A matching 128-thread target block and source tile halves the dynamic shared-memory footprint versus the prior 256-thread variant, while staging only force-relevant source fields reduces each tile to 16 bytes per particle. The smaller tile also doubles CTA count for a given N and doubles the number of tile iterations, so any benefit from reduced resource use or increased CTA availability may be offset by lower source reuse and more barriers; the official measurements must decide.

retained: Use a 128-thread CTA and matching 128-particle source chunks; set items_per_block to 128 to keep the launch configuration compatible and preserve complete target coverage.
Stage only source x, y, z, and mass in a compact shared-memory structure, reserving 2048 dynamic shared-memory bytes per CTA.

Keep one target and one force accumulator per active thread; all threads participate in both barriers, partial source tiles are bounded, self-interactions are excluded by global index, and inactive tail threads do not write output.
